subject: geography
title: Drainage Basin: Stores Fill in Sequence, the River Lags

questions.prompt: During one storm over a drainage basin, how does the rain reach the river?

choices.text: It runs straight off the surface into the river, so discharge peaks with the heaviest rain
It reaches the river only through the groundwater store, so there is no surface flow at all
It is held by stores that fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates
It is all evaporated, so the river only rises days later

questions.misconception: The river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river. In fact The basin stores fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates, so discharge peaks after the peak rain and then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow.

questions.prompt: Which store fills first when the storm arrives, and what does the hydrograph do while it fills?

choices.text: The soil store fills first, and discharge rises at once
The interception store fills first, and the channel and hydrograph stay flat
The groundwater store fills first, and the recession begins
No store fills, and discharge peaks immediately

questions.explanation: Scene 1 works this: the interception store catches the rain first and only begins to spill once it is full, so the channel and the hydrograph stay flat.

questions.prompt: A student says the river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river. Explain, in two sentences, what actually happens to the rain on its way to the channel.
questions.answer: The basin stores fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates, so discharge peaks after the peak rain and then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to trace the pulse store by store: each store must fill before water passes on, and fast surface flow only begins at soil saturation, which is why the discharge peak lags the rain peak.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what switches on when the soil store saturates and what it does to discharge.
questions.answer: When the soil store saturates, overland flow switches on and runs over the surface to the channel, so discharge rises fast and peaks after the rain has already eased.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows saturation switching on overland flow: discharge rises fast and peaks late, after the rain itself has eased and shrunk.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of the storm pulse in order?

choices.text: Interception fills first and spills, the soil store fills next, percolation feeds groundwater last, the soil saturates and overland flow peaks the river late, then baseflow sustains a slow recession
Overland flow peaks the river with the heaviest rain, then interception fills, then the soil store dries out
Groundwater fills first, the soil store saturates before any rain is intercepted, discharge peaks before the rain
The river recedes on baseflow first, then the storm arrives and interception fills

questions.explanation: Scene 1 fills interception first, scene 2 fills the soil store and starts groundwater last, scene 3 saturates the soil so overland flow peaks the river late, and scene 4 recedes slowly on baseflow.
